A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Minimal Pair-Based Evaluation of Code-Switching. All 24 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original bilingual judgments, benchmark evaluations of language models, processing-error analysis and part-of-speech analyses (Sections 2–3; Appendices B–E).

after.justification: v2 retains these original human-validation and language-model results, including the numerical evaluations in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 retain the same processing pipeline and minimal-pair construction, including translation near switch points, preserving switch counts and restricting lexical changes. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: The same 11 language pairs remain, covering tweet-derived code-switching and Turkish–German and Chinese–English speech transcriptions. Task requirements and dataset coverage in Table 4 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Section 3.1 and Tables 5–10 retain the same BLOOM, Qwen2.5, Llama-3, OLMo, EuroLLM and XLM-RoBERTa configurations. Human and random reference comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Sampling, temporal splits, filtering thresholds, model precision and scoring procedures are unchanged. Changing 'less than 6 tokens' to 'fewer than 6 tokens' in Section 2.1 does not revise the filtering threshold.

E4.justification: Both retain the 100-pair German–English processing-error analysis, human–LLM margin analysis, part-of-speech analyses in Appendix B and disagreement examples in Appendix C.13. No analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: The paired and unpaired permutation tests retain 10,000 resamples and alpha = 0.05. Significance reporting and margin-distribution displays are unchanged, with no changes to run counts, seeds or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative findings match throughout, including Tables 1–2 and 5–10 and the result figures. Llama-3.1 405B's German–English accuracy remains 74.8%, and human inter-annotator agreement remains kappa = 0.57.

T1.justification: The accuracy and log-probability-margin definitions in Section 3.1 are identical. Assumptions underlying minimal-pair construction are retained, and no mathematical result, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same benchmark, human-validation, model-scale and closed-class-word claims. Their scientific scope and strength do not change.

C2.justification: Interpretations of human–LLM agreement, model scaling and Chinese–English performance are retained. Limitations concerning noisy data, processing errors, participant representativeness, multilingual code-switching and possible training-data overlap are unchanged.

D1.justification: The preprocessing instructions, named tools, data splits, GPU and quantization details, and benchmark/corpus/code access link remain unchanged. Appendix A's caption spelling correction supplies no new technical information.

R1.justification: The same works are cited with unchanged research positioning. Updates specify preprint versions for existing BabyLM and MultiBLiMP references and add publication details and a link for the existing Sterner and Teufel (2025) reference.

P1.justification: v2 adds Sterner's current-affiliation note and makes isolated wording, spelling and bibliographic edits, including 'guided by' and 'licenses'. Section order and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The affiliation footnote and local text edits produce limited reflow on the opening pages. Table 3's caption corrects 'Wikitionary' to 'Wiktionary'; figures, table structures and appendix layouts otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The affiliation note, isolated copyedits and bibliographic updates provide limited editorial polish. The methodology, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations are unchanged, and these small edits do not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
